question: What does one who knows thus see all verse-gatha-etc as?
premises: Verse-gatha-etc joined with beginning and end is whatever.
Knowing thus, one sees all as mantra indeed.
inference: All verse-gatha-etc joined with beginning and end is seen as mantra by one who knows thus.
uncertainties: The compound ślokagāthādi may include further verse-types beyond verse and gāthā.
The exact scope of ādimāntyayutaṃ as beginning-end joined is not fully explicit.
The relation of tataḥ and tasmād is not fully disambiguated.
plain_english: Whatever verse, gāthā, or the like is joined with beginning and end, therefore, knowing thus, one sees all as mantra indeed.
